notes: This index points to normative properties in the RFCs; it does not replace them. A vector id is a stable label, not a pointer: the CT-Rn prefix records where the id was first filed, and the rfc column states the clause the vector rests on. CT-R5 vectors rest on RFC-1 and RFC-4 clauses; CT-R4-011 to CT-R4-013 rest on the manuscript; CT-R4-004a and CT-R4-004b rest on the RFC-4 v0.3 revision, ratified on 19 November 2026 and kept outside the frozen baseline; CT-R4-015 and CT-R4-016 rest on RFC-2 and RFC-5 clauses as read by RN-001. IMPLEMENTED means a behavioral test exists in the current runner. DECLARED means the RFC specifies the property but the runner does not test it. RESERVED means the check is identified but the RFC does not specify it. For CT-R4-004a and CT-R4-004b, the RFC is the ratified RFC-4 v0.3 revision.

The runner registers 61 vector IDs (23 core/commit, of which three lifecycle vectors, three registered under RN-001 §3 and since superseded, and two registered under the RFC-4 v0.3 revision of 19 November 2026, and 38 extended). Registration alone does not make a vector IMPLEMENTED: 36 extended entries currently return an implementation-gap result without exercising the property. The archived v0.3.1 reports also contain false PASS assessments for C3, CT-R4-005, CT-R4-009, and CT-R4-010; use corrected implementation and current report before making conformance claims.

status_definitions.IMPLEMENTED: a behavioral test exists in the current runner.
status_definitions.DECLARED: the RFC specifies the property but the runner does not test it.
status_definitions.RESERVED: the check is identified but the RFC does not specify it.

rows_without_vector.normative_property: Signature verification must be based on canonicalized payloads, not JSON formatting.
Reuse of an idempotency key with a modified action must be rejected.
Requests outside the declared freshness window must be rejected.
A credential signed by a revoked key past its revocation bound must not authorize execution.
UNKNOWN evidence must not be treated as satisfying an invariant; default to HOLD or HARD_VETO.
STALE measurements must be excluded; a critical stale measurement yields HOLD or HARD_VETO.
MISSING evidence must remain distinguishable from other epistemic states.
CONTRADICTORY evidence yields HOLD unless a deterministic, pre-declared resolution applies.
LOW CONFIDENCE must invoke Conservative Admissibility.
The membrane must not invent observations; observations without provenance are invalid for structural evaluation.
Measurements must carry provenance and required contextual bindings.
Interpretations must be produced by deterministic, versioned mappings.
Decisions must derive only from Interpretation and applicable Invariants.
Prohibited inferences must not be used to establish admissibility.
A reason chain must link the decision to interpretations and exact measurements for deterministic reproduction.
Uncertainty must be evaluated against worst-case plausible bounds.
Increasing uncertainty must never expand the Admissible Region.
A hard invariant violation must bypass scoring and produce HARD_VETO.
Confidence modulation may only degrade, never upgrade, the disposition.
Credentials must be checked using public cryptographic material or sufficiently fresh local revocation data.
Verification must not depend on synchronous real-time IAM lookups at the Execution Boundary.
Child authority scope must not exceed parent scope; invalid chain links invalidate descendants.
Credential revocation, policy invocation, context drift, and execution invocation must remain distinct events.
Revocation bounds must be explicit, versioned, and signed.
Revocation after grant but before/during commit must trigger HARD_VETO and a safe-state transition.
Parent revocation and material authority/context changes must invalidate or trigger re-evaluation of affected standing.
Composition must preserve local Standing; recovery must establish a new authorization context.
τ_K and exhaustion behavior must be pre-declared; HOLD expiry defaults to fail-closed, and Shadow Mode requires bounded review capacity.

claims_policy.title: What a REG conformance result lets you say
claims_policy.status_line: Two sections are in force: "What counts as an admission" and "Third-party assessments", ratified by the author on 18 November 2026. The rest is not yet in force.

sections.title: What a run establishes
parts: Which set the test belongs to
What a result does not establish
paragraphs: One run covers one revision of one subject, reached in one way, on the cases the suite contains. Three things are reported separately and must stay separate when a result is quoted.
Only PASS counts as a pass.

Which set the test belongs to. REG vectors test properties specified by the REG RFCs. Effect probes (HX-EFFECT-*) check that a refusal matches zero downstream effects and an allowed call exactly one. Property checks (PX-*) each exercise one property that the index lists and that has no executable vector yet. Probes and property checks are listed apart and are never counted among the vectors.

The reading by property. A run also groups its results by candidate property family: the vectors, the probes and the property checks that exercise the same property are counted together, each under its own kind. The families are candidates and are not part of the frozen RFCs. The grouping changes no outcome and no vector count. It shows which properties were observed on a subject whose shape does not fit the vectors as written.

What a result does not establish. Each test declares where it observes, as a phase of RFC-0 §5, and what its result leaves open. A test submits one case: a pass is a pass on that case. Tests that depend on time use the bound the subject declares and none of their own; when the subject declares no bound, the test does not run. "No effect" is read from one journal, after the effect window the port declares. verdict.json carries all of this for every result that gave an observation.

What counts as an admission. RFC-0 §4 lets execution proceed on PASS and on FLAG, the latter only under an explicit condition or supervision. A test that needs an admitted action accepts either. The run lists the tests that went forward on a FLAG and says whether the condition was observed.

As ratified in RN-001 §1: a FLAG that carries an explicit condition counts as an admission. A FLAG that carries none does not satisfy RFC-0 §4; it is recorded as an implementation gap, and a quote of a test that went forward on it says so.

rows: A documented correspondence. No product behaviour demonstrated.
Real product behaviour, observed through a port.
The runtime satisfies the properties natively. No run reaches this today.
The test could not reach a determinate result.
The property cannot apply to this runtime.

sections.title: How to quote a result
paragraphs: A statement about a result names all of the following:

A count of families is quoted with the words "candidate families" and with the number not exercised. If a test went forward on a FLAG whose condition was not observed, the quote says so. A quote that rests on one test's result gives what that test does not establish.
quotes: <subject> <version> at commit <commit>, run with reg-conformance at <commit>, evidence level 2: 0 of 59 REG vectors executed (59 adapter required); 4 of 4 effect probes passed. By property: 2 of 14 candidate families with a passing check, none with a failing check, 12 not exercised. Bundle: <link>.
steps: the subject and its exact revision (commit),
the counts per outcome, with vectors, probes and property checks apart,
where the evidence bundle is, with its checksums.

sections.title: What must not be said
bullets: That a subject is "REG-conformant", "REG-certified" or "REG-compliant" on the strength of a run. verdict.json always carries certifying: false.
That a result at level 1 describes a product. The 15 passes of the bundled reference kernel are not results of any runtime.
That a result holds for another revision of the subject. Another commit is another run.
That a pass count is a score. Tests that were not executed are not passes and are not failures.
That a result maps to a regulation or to another framework. The crosswalk states such relations one by one, each with its limit.
That an effect probe or a property check is a REG vector, or the reverse.
That a row of the index is "covered" or "implemented" because a property check exists for it. The row keeps its status in VECTORS.md.
That a property holds "at the declared bound" for a subject that declares none. The test did not run.
That no observed effect means no effect. The journal is one channel, read after one declared window.
That a family with a passing check is satisfied, or that a subject "satisfies" a number of families. One check observed one behaviour.

sections.title: Mappings written by someone other than the runtime's owner
paragraphs: A port translates a runtime's verdicts and refusals into REG terms. When the port was not written or reviewed by the runtime's owner, the result is provisional and is quoted as such until the owner has confirmed or corrected the mapping.

sections.title: Third-party assessments
paragraphs: A third party may run the suite and report its results under the terms above. A third party's own requirement identifiers, scoring or labels are that party's work. REG neither defines nor endorses them. An assessment report keeps the two apart: what the REG run observed, and what the assessor concluded from it.
What an assessment says about REG is limited to this sentence:
followed by the quote described in "How to quote a result", and nothing more.
quotes: Assessed against REG Conformance <version> at commit <commit>, evidence level <N>.
bullets: A readiness, maturity or assurance rating defined by the assessor is not a REG conformance level, and is not presented as one. In particular, a "readiness" result says nothing about conformance.
Using the REG name in a commercial offer, product or service name requires the licensor's written agreement. Apache-2.0 covers the files, not the name (see below).
